LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT- POTTERY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.4: Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are clay items dried under the shade?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify pottery items made using slab technique
2. model a vase using slab technique for expression
3. appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT- POTTERY
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT- POTTERY
Study Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify pottery items made using slab technique

What this means
In this part you learn to identify pottery items made using slab technique. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify pottery items made using slab technique.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify pottery items made using slab technique. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Model a vase using slab technique for expression

What this means
In this part you learn to model a vase using slab technique for expression. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: model a vase using slab technique for expression.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can model a vase using slab technique for expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify pottery items made using slab technique)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery in your own words. (skill: model a vase using slab technique for expression)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify pottery items made using slab technique.
3. Practise this skill: model a vase using slab technique for expression.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate pottery as an indigenous Kenyan craft.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are clay items dried under the shade?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Indigenous Kenyan Craft- Pottery means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify pottery items made using slab technique.
5. Be able to: model a vase using slab technique for expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
